q-sop-04.Not reportable, since alarm age is outsi: Before trusting an exclusion, find its wording. Reread the SOP's limitations list and ask whether it says what this option claims.

q-sop-05.In the hallway outside the bedrooms and: That pattern matches an older code edition. Open IRC section R314.3 and compare its location list with each remaining option.
q-sop-05.In each bedroom and in the kitchen, but: IRC R314.3.3 keeps alarms a set distance from cooking appliances because of nuisance alarms. Ask how this option's kitchen alarm squares with that.

q-sop-08.Acceptable, provided the flap is rigid p: Rigid and self-closing describe how the flap moves. Reread the course's garage-to-house door standard for what that door must be, then judge.
q-sop-08.Cosmetic damage to the door, which the S: Cosmetic covers marks that change only appearance. Ask whether an opening cut through the full thickness of a door fits that definition.

q-sop-10.Flexible duct with a foil jacket, sealed: Ask where your belief about foil-jacketed flex in garages came from. Which section of the course's garage standard covers ducts?
q-sop-10.Ductboard or flex, provided the penetrat: Fire caulk at a penetration is a real detail. Reread the course's garage separation standard in full and test each remaining option against it.

q-sop-19.200 hours: 80 classroom and 120 field, i: Ask yourself where that breakdown came from. Reread 11 NCAC 08 .1021 and write down its figures before comparing options.

q-sop-29.Describe, Diagnose, Implication, Disclos: Ask yourself where that expansion came from. Find DDID in the NC Board's study guide and check each of the four words.

q-ea-01.Acceptable, as long as both conductors a: Ask where that same-gauge rule came from. Reread the course's electrical panel section on conductors at breaker terminals before choosing.

q-ea-04.When the panel is a subpanel, where whit: A subpanel still keeps its neutrals on their own isolated bar. Ask whether that makes white and black interchangeable there.

q-ea-06.Signs of a lightning strike or surge, an: Lightning damage usually shows as scorching, pitting, or melted parts. Ask whether the stem describes any of that before choosing among the rest.

q-ea-14.Combined on one bar, the same way as in: Rules written for the main panel follow from its role as the service. Ask whether a subpanel shares that role, then reread the subpanel section.

q-er-05.Acceptable, because the receptacle still: Ask yourself what result your tester actually showed, and whether 'it powers devices' answers that result or a different question.
q-er-05.Correct it yourself with a three-to-two: Ask yourself what an adapter plug changes inside the wall, then reread the course's section on ungrounded three-prong receptacles.
q-er-05.Acceptable if a surge protector is plugg: Ask where the belief that a surge strip offsets an open ground came from. Reread the course's receptacle testing section before choosing.

q-er-10.Fire hazard; recommend rewiring the atti: Ask whether an inspector's report should prescribe a whole-attic rewire, or leave the repair scope to the trade. Then weigh the rest.

q-er-11.Stranded aluminum service entrance condu: Ask yourself where that idea came from. Reread NC .1110(c) and note the exact wiring type it names.

q-er-13.Disposals are plug-in appliances, which: Ask where the plug-in exclusion idea came from. Reread the SOP's appliance and electrical limitations, and see what they actually exclude.

q-ca-03.Recommend a dehumidifier sized for the c: Ask where the dehumidifier-only idea came from. Reread the course's crawlspace section on standing water before choosing.

q-ca-06.Leave it out of the report entirely, bec: Ask where the leave-it-out idea came from. Find the NC SOP's pest wording and read it exactly before choosing.

q-ca-07.It is cosmetic, as long as the insulatio: Ask whether the stem's condition is about appearance at all. Reread how the course defines cosmetic, then weigh the rest.
q-ca-07.Flex duct is designed to rest on the soi: Ask where the idea of resting flex duct on soil came from. Check the manufacturer's installation guidance or the course's duct section.

q-ap-05.Not reportable, since the hood was worki: A passing operation test settles one question. Ask whether a report also describes how a component is designed, then weigh the rest.

q-ef-02.Runoff will slowly erode the mulch beds: Ask yourself whether mulch erosion is the main stake, then reread the NC exterior section's wording on grading and drainage.

q-eh-03.Both standards require testing the seal: Ask whether a visual home inspection tests seals on every window, then reread the window wording in the NC and InterNACHI SOPs.

q-eh-04.It slopes inward toward the sash so rain: Picture rain landing on that sill. Ask where gravity takes it on an inward slope, and whether the house wants water there.

q-eh-05.It is excluded, so you leave it out of t: Ask where the leave-it-out idea came from. Reread the exact wording of NC .1109 on backflow before choosing.

q-eh-07.Acceptable; a handrail is required start: Ask yourself where the figure of 6 came from. Which course section covers handrails on stairs, and what riser count does it give?

q-fp-05.A Level I visual inspection by the homeo: Ask yourself who is qualified to perform a chimney inspection under NFPA 211, and whether a homeowner fits that role.

q-fp-08.Nothing; caps are decorative and optiona: Ask where the idea that caps are only decorative came from. Reread the course's chimney section on caps before choosing.

q-hv-02.Upward toward the chimney at least 1 in: The 1 in per foot figure overstates the code minimum. Recheck the minimum slope figure in the course's vent connector section.

q-mo-08.As mold growth that needs remediation by: Ask yourself where the mold call came from. Reread NC's limitations section and the course's moisture reporting guidance, then decide.
q-mo-08.As acceptable, since crawlspace wood oft: Ask where the idea that 24 percent is normal came from. Check the course's moisture meter section for its framing thresholds.

q-ai-01.Its R-value and the year it was installe: Ask where R-value and install year came from. Reread InterNACHI's attic and insulation section and list exactly what it says to describe.

q-ai-10.Repair item; recommend sanding and repai: Ask where the repaint call came from. Reread the general limitations in the NC SOP, then judge the stem's details again.

q-dk-01.Monitor it, unless the ledger is visibly: Ask where the monitor approach came from. Reread the course's deck section on ledger connections before choosing.

q-dk-04.Acceptable if most of the holes are fill: Ask where the idea that most holes is enough came from. Check a hanger maker's installation instructions before choosing.

q-rt-02.It matters on new roofs still under warr: Ask whether a warranty changes what an inspector reports, or only who pays for the fix. Then reread the course's tile roof section.

q-rt-04.The tiles themselves, which are fully wa: Ask where the idea that tile alone is waterproof came from. Reread the course's tile roof section on what each layer does.

q-eg-07.A door from the garage into an inside ha: Ask where the concern about hallway doors came from. Reread the 25 Standards garage section and what it says about each opening.
